name: Synchronous condenser
summary: An unloaded synchronous machine on the network that supplies reactive power, inertia and short-circuit strength.
description: A synchronous condenser is a synchronous machine running without a prime mover, connected to the network to supply or absorb reactive power by adjusting its field current. Because it is a real rotating machine it also contributes inertia and high short-circuit current, which converter-dominated networks often lack.

Single-line diagrams draw a synchronous machine circle labelled SC or with a capacitor-like note, connected through a step-up transformer and breaker, with a starting arrangement such as a pony motor or static frequency converter. A flywheel may be shown on the shaft to add inertia.

The symbol looks like a generator but the machine exports no active power and draws a small amount to cover losses. It does not show the starting method, inertia constant or overexcitation limits, which define how much it helps during faults.
readingNotes: There is no prime mover; a pony motor or static starter is used only to bring the machine up to speed.
Check for a flywheel added to raise inertia.
drawingChecklist: State Mvar range, inertia and short-circuit contribution.
distinction: A synchronous condenser exchanges only reactive power; a synchronous generator also delivers active power from a prime mover.
